executiveSummary: Maasdriel's official/generated 2025 identity, 26,289 residents, 24 neighbourhoods, five districts, ten BAG woonplaatsen, 21 BRT settlement labels, six road-border records and 49 scheduled-transit stop areas are substantially coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 26,275 residents, fourteen below the municipality control (-0.053%), which the allocator reconciles without rewriting published observations. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with finite bounds, exact zero-event behavior, causal-ledger closure, service-layer invariance and monotone event-attributable burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Maasdriel lies in a system of distinct Bommelerwaard, Alem and Heerewaarden flood compartments between the Waal, Maas and Afgedamde Maas, but the generic river run selects no river boundary, dike trajectory/state, breach, LIWO footprint, arrival or recession; instead it holds an exact 2.252815 floodDepthM and 0.706022 severity from T+12 through T+72, reports 13,033 affected people-equivalent and 912,171.227 cumulative deprived person-hours at T+72, and ranks Hedel 23rd and Alem 17th of 24. Eight nonzero single-hazard T+24 outputs reuse the exact same neighbourhood order despite different river, rain/sewer, heat, wind, smoke and cyber mechanisms. Public registers add 244 partial water objects, one electricity-planning sample, 47 antenna sites and thirteen education locations, but none provides complete operational topology, state, backup or restoration. The A2 crosses both the Waal and Maas, N322 is another cross-compartment route, rail traverses the municipality without a station, and acute emergency departments are external; static geometry cannot prove evacuation, responder, supply or care access. Maasdriel explicitly says no emergency support point exists yet and identifies the Kerkdriel town hall only as a current contact fallback, not a shelter. Missing support capacity, household stock, care acceptance, operator state and long-horizon water/air/weather observations remain Unknown or NoData, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0263 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The annual official/generated row identifies GM0263 as Maasdriel and reports 26,289 residents, density 399/km², 21.1% aged 65-plus and 3,630 one-person households. CBS/PDOK context is CC BY 4.0 and demographic context, not current occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The reference point [5.31012938251282,51.77739166960411] lies inside the 2025 generalized MultiPolygon. Its 107 coordinate positions make it a display/selection outline rather than a hydraulic compartment, terrain, sewer, forest, road or asset mask.

Twenty-four neighbourhood rows in five districts sum to 26,275 residents (-14, -0.053%), 11,345 households and 5,570 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. The simulator reconciles population to the municipality control without silently treating the difference as zero people.

BAG supplies ten woonplaatsen—Alem, Ammerzoden, Hedel, Heerewaarden, Hoenzadriel, Hurwenen, Kerkdriel, Rossum, Velddriel and Well—and BRT 21 locality labels. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; labels, polygons and population rows retain distinct provenance and meaning.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current rain, sewer, climate-adaptation and heat-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; Water- en Rioleringsplan Bommelerwaard 2022–2026; Lokaal Hitteplan Bommelerwaard 2022–2025
supports: The municipality says short intense rain can overload the still-combined rainwater/wastewater pipes and that it is adding separate rainwater pipes. Its water-overload page warns that streets and in some cases buildings can flood, road water can contain sewage, displaced covers create hazards and pumping is ineffective while receiving water remains high.

Maasdriel allocates water responsibilities among municipality, Waterschap Rivierenland, Province Gelderland, Vitens/Dunea and owners. This establishes different accountable systems; it does not publish sewer catchments, pipe connectivity, capacity, pump telemetry, drinking-water pressure/quality or restoration state.

The municipality participates in Klimaat Actief Rivierenland and identifies heavier rain, heat, drought and water-level change as distinct adaptation mechanisms. Static adaptation context is not a current observation, probability, forecast or incident footprint.

The currently linked local heat plan is explicitly 2022–2025 and coordinates municipality, GGD Gelderland-Zuid, Red Cross and local partners around activation of the national heat plan and outreach to vulnerable residents. No successor or live activation state was found; an expired planning period is not an active T+72 action. No standard reuse licence or machine update cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Bommelerwaard managed-water system, partial assets and timestamped Waterinfo context
evidenceSources.edition: Current peilbesluit project page inspected 3 September 2026; existing decision 2018 under review in 2026–2028; HWH retrieved 3 September 2026; Waterinfo observations 2 September and forecasts 3 September 2026
supports: The water board describes a roughly 27,000-hectare management area enclosed by the Waal and Maas that includes the Bommelerwaard plus the separate Heerewaarden, Alem and Bern polders. Its extensive network of ditches, waterways, weirs and pumps supports both water supply and discharge for villages, agriculture and nature.

The partial HWH assignment contains 244 points in GM0263: 213 weirs, 21 surface-water pumps, nine wastewater pumps and Sint Andries sluice. Registered functions include both supply and discharge; missing function/capacity, duplicate/co-located objects and a registered capacity of zero retain source semantics and cannot be converted into operational zero flow.

The HWH registers are contributor-dependent national inventories, retrieved 3 September 2026 under CC BY-SA 4.0. They do not establish complete connectivity, direction, compatible capacity units, control logic, telemetry, power dependency, live availability, backup or restoration.

No Waterinfo point is assigned inside the municipal polygon. Nearby 2 September observations include Empel beneden 45 cm NAP and Zaltbommel 73 cm NAP; the rolling forecast includes Hedel at 44/39/50/64/75 cm NAP for T+1/+6/+12/+24/+48 but no national T+72 water-level features. Waterinfo is CC0, public/non-mission-critical and point-based; neighbour assignment and missing horizon are not zero water, defence safety or a municipal inundation surface.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current regional crisis, flood-evacuation and health-chain planning
evidenceSources.edition: Zorgrisicoprofiel definitive and adopted 25 April 2024; Regionaal Beleidsplan and Crisisplan 2024–2027 adopted 21 December 2023; public dike-failure/overstroming plan inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The 2024 care-risk profile selects high-river flooding, drinking-water contamination, electricity loss, ICT/telecom loss and a toxic shipping incident as five priority scenarios. It records staff reachability, bed/material/staff buffers, cross-institution evacuation agreements, information management and acute access under flooding as unresolved care-chain issues.

The profile says high river levels can be foreseen days ahead but breach location is difficult to predict. It explicitly distinguishes an advisory/evacuation phase from post-breach access and care effects; its Bemmel scenario must not be projected spatially onto Maasdriel.

The public flood response plan includes separate dike rings 38 Bommelerwaard, 39 Alem and 40 Heerewaarden and municipality-specific pickup/evacuation routes, including A2/N322 approaches for Kerkdriel/Velddriel and the Hedel A2/Oude Rijksweg/Baronieweg route. A plan route is not proof that a road is incident-passable or that vehicles, staff and destination capacity are available.

Regional plans are official scenario/coordination evidence with multi-year validity, not current warnings, defence states, evacuation orders or live resource commitments. No standard redistribution licence or machine incident cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO scenario evidence and primary-defence trajectory semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Current LIWO information page and statutory/factsheet context inspected 3 September 2026; native scenario editions vary by layer
supports: LIWO is the WMCN system of professional map layers for preparing for water nuisance and floods. IPLO warns that correct interpretation requires specialist water-manager knowledge; a maximum-depth layer is not self-selecting operational truth.

Public national primary-defence documentation distinguishes trajectories 38-1 Bommelerwaard-Waal, 38-2 Bommelerwaard-Maas, 39-1 Alem and 40-1/40-2 Heerewaarden. They cannot be collapsed into one municipality-wide river-depth scalar.

EU flood-risk products distinguish large, medium and small probability scenario classes; individual breach locations, source rivers, boundary conditions, defence assumptions, arrival, depth, velocity and recession must remain attached to each scenario.

LIWO access/terms and individual layer edition, resolution, valid scope, NoData/mask and licence must be captured at ingestion. An uncovered cell, unselected breach or absent layer remains Unknown/not selected, not safe or zero depth.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Gelderland / ProRail / OVapi / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Bridge, road, rail, transit and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; official operator pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Six monthly CC0 NWB border records reduce to four numbered physical identities: A2, N322, N831 and N832. A2 and N322 appear on two municipal sides and are series/crossing dependencies, not additive capacity; each 260/150 scenario-unit ceiling is a logical mobility/supply proxy rather than measured throughput.

The A2 crosses the Waal at Zaltbommel and the Maas near Hedel/Empel; N322 is the principal east–west regional connection. Rijkswaterstaat's August 2026 closure between Kerkdriel and Empel produced an official detour of up to 60 minutes, demonstrating time-sensitive dependence without implying a current closure in this audit.

The Utrecht–'s-Hertogenbosch railway traverses Maasdriel and crosses the same river system, but no ProRail station lies inside GM0263; Zaltbommel and 's-Hertogenbosch are the relevant external stations. Forty-nine in-boundary GTFS stop areas are schedule/reference context, not live vehicles, accessible capacity or evacuation transport.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 has no emergency department in GM0263. Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis is 10.55 km and Ziekenhuis Rivierenland 14.41 km straight-line from the municipality point and both report 24/7 emergency departments; questionnaire status and distance do not establish route travel time, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, diversion or backup endurance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Maasdriel / Liander / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Current 72-hour preparedness and partial electricity, communication and school context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal page and April 2026 Liander cooperation notice inspected 3 September 2026; deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Maasdriel asks households to prepare for at least 72 hours with water, food, medicines, radio, power bank, cash, meeting point and routes. It explicitly says no emergency support point yet exists; the municipality hall in Kerkdriel is the current contact fallback, possible extra functions remain under investigation, and a support point is not a shelter.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander area OS ZALTBOMMEL 10-1i and reports 64 MW existing/46 MW required withdrawal capacity, a 19.7 MW/76-request withdrawal queue, 76 MW/42-request injection queue, 28 projects and earliest year 2030. This open-data planning sample is not full municipal coverage, live load, outage, reserve, switching or restoration; exact dataset licence identifier was not found.

The municipality and Liander announced neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood grid reinforcement expected from end-2027 and acknowledge existing momentary flicker/outage and capacity pressure. A construction programme is not an incident-time feeder map or availability promise.

RDI assigns 47 installations—24 mobile, eleven fixed-link and twelve amateur—and DUO assigns thirteen education locations—eleven primary and two other registered education uses. RDI states no standard reuse licence/fixed cadence; DUO is attribution licensed and daily. Neither register establishes coverage/backhaul/power, present occupancy, shelter/support role, accessibility, capacity, stock, staffing or operation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Zuid / Waterschap Rivierenland / KNMI / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Other local hazard pathways, agriculture/water quality and monitoring gaps
evidenceSources.edition: VRGZ planning period 2024–2027; WSRL 2025 water-quality results published 20 July 2026; monitoring snapshots 2 September 2026
supports: VRGZ treats high-river flooding, extreme weather, heat, electricity, telecom/ICT/cyber, hazardous transport/shipping and nature fire near vulnerable objects as relevant regional planning categories; regional eligibility is not a GM0263 event probability, footprint or current warning.

WSRL describes Bommelerwaard agriculture, fruit growing, arable farming, dairy and greenhouse cultivation as important managed-water users. It reported the region's highest 2025 pesticide-limit exceedances in greenhouse-area surface water despite a collective greenhouse sewer. Water quantity, water quality, agriculture and logistics are distinct service/exposure pathways.

No KNMI weather station, RIVM PM2.5 point or 365-day KNMI seismic origin lies inside GM0263. Herwijnen weather is nearest at 14.43 km, Nistelrode PM2.5 at 18.32 km and a reviewed M0.77 Heel event at 77.69 km. KNMI is CC BY 4.0; current RIVM air values are indicative hourly points with no standard reuse licence stated.

The canonical coastal preset has zero direct water and is a wind exercise here; the Groningen-style earthquake is a remote exercise; canonical wildfire supplies only remote smoke and no local flame. No-match and remote forcing are not zero local weather, smoke exposure, ground susceptibility, ignition likelihood or all-hazard safety.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong official flood, water-chain, care and 72-hour context exists, but incident selection and operational readiness remain unconfirmed.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0263 pnpm audit:model passed two tests across severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Focused inline Vite runs captured the complete six-checkpoint trajectories and neighbourhood rankings without creating a scratch file.

These are deterministic exercise indices, modeled people-equivalent and matched-no-event service person-hours—not observations, probabilities, measured customer outages, casualties, economic loss or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal closure and cumulative-burden contracts pass.
notes: All eight availability values remain in [0,1], while hazard dimensions, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero event hazard, affected population and event-attributable burden; repeats are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 24 neighbourhoods and exactly 26,289 residents; local demand/delivery reconcile and changing selected service leaves hazard unchanged.
Arithmetic validity does not validate hydraulic, route, utility, care, occupancy, intervention or recovery meaning.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common source-insensitive neighbourhood seed contradicts Maasdriel's compartment, rain/sewer, heat and smoke/fire geography.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all use the exact full 24-neighbourhood order, starting Overige verspreide huizen, Wellseind-Slijkwell, Verspreide huizen Hurwenen en Rossum and Verspreide huizen in het bouwgebied.

River ranks separate Heerewaarden 10th, Alem 17th, Hedel 23rd and the Hedel polder 24th without choosing a Waal, Maas or Afgedamde Maas event, defence trajectory or connected footprint. The order cannot be validated as a flood scenario.
The same order ranks local rain, heat and remote smoke despite different catchment/sewer, paving/shade/vulnerability and plume mechanisms.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts derives hazardSeed from city seed, scenario seed and region id without disaster family, source containment or evidence surface. Administrative identifiers and hashes are not substitutes for selected physical geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Road-only transfer is correctly scoped, but exact managed-water, wastewater, utility, telecom, facility and supply states lack physical evidence.
notes: The six NWB records affect mobility and road logistics/supply only, avoiding false physical utility equivalence; their capacities and recoveries remain scenario proxies without event-valid passability.

Primary flood defence, polder supply/drainage, sewer conveyance, wastewater treatment and potable pressure/quality are distinct. HWH points and Waterinfo stations do not connect or operate these systems.

Liander planning, antenna, school, ProRail/GTFS and hospital records do not expose complete topology, switching, backhaul, priority customers, staff, stock, vehicle, generator, acceptance or restoration state.

At river T+72 availability is drainage 0.295371, water 0.387439, telecom 0.418751, power 0.439916, facilities 0.357239, gas 0.678477, mobility 0.749419 and supply 0.799407. No authority validates these exact values.

causalTrace.summary: The arithmetic ledger closes, but event selection, evidence time and accountable first-72-hour actions are absent from the causal graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service-stage contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure closes numerically.

The river path selects no river/gauge/datum/hydrograph, defence trajectory/state, breach/overtopping, probability class, footprint, arrival or recession. The 2.252815 floodDepthM property must not be shown as a sourced municipal metre prediction.
Trace does not select rain duration/catchment/sewer state, polder control, potable quality/advisory, route/bridge/rail state, hospital acceptance, heat-plan activation, plume or named cyber target.

T+0–6 needs evidence/event selection, warnings and coordination; T+6–24 defence/evacuation/closure/care decisions; T+24–48 verified access, water, care, logistics and utility status; T+48–72 dewatering/repair, welfare, re-entry and unresolved-needs review. Each action needs owner, trigger, request, confirmation, resource, execution, verification, expiry and rollback.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood effects are conservative, but exact plateaus and recoveries are not tied to a Maasdriel event, operators, access or confirmed actions.
notes: River floodDepthM/severity stays exactly 2.252815/0.706022 from T+12 through T+72; seven services are unchanged T+24–T+72 while facilities falls from 0.544893 to 0.357239, affected rises 12,060 to 13,033 and burden reaches 912,171.227 person-hours without selected hydraulics or a recovery plan.

Compound holds floodDepthM 0.451672 from T+12 through T+72; severity declines 0.924910 to 0.490112 but affected stays 13,865 and burden reaches 956,268.737, while T+72 telecom remains 0.259597 and water 0.351314 without operator calibration.

Storm/pluvial/winter direct hazard is zero by T+48 while person-hours continue accumulating during modeled recovery. A zero current forcing is not a safe-state statement; drainage, contamination, displacement, access and repair can persist.

No active support-point capacity, household stock, care-home/pharmacy status, emergency-water distribution, utility switching, fuel/spares, crew milestone, crossing state or hospital acceptance is ingested. Seventy-two-hour preparedness is not a restoration deadline or aid guarantee.

findings.summary: Eight materially different nonzero single-hazard scenarios reuse one complete neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank all 24 neighbourhoods identically, led by Overige verspreide huizen and Wellseind-Slijkwell and ending with Hedel and its polder. The model seed omits disaster family, source geometry and evidence coverage, contradicting the distinct official defence, rain/sewer, heat, smoke and cyber mechanisms in E02–E05/E08.
findings.action: V3 release gate: replace the common rank with hazard-specific full-geometry surfaces and explicit coverage/NoData. Add regression tests that physically different hazards need not share an order and that source-containing/covered cells govern direct impact; preserve service-layer invariance.

findings.summary: A physically plausible major-river threat is presented with unsupported municipal depth, footprint and timing precision.
findings.evidence: E03–E05 distinguish Waal, Maas, Afgedamde Maas and trajectories 38-1, 38-2, 39-1, 40-1/40-2 plus multiple polders. The model selects none, yet floodDepthM 2.252815 and severity 0.706022 persist T+12–T+72, river T+72 reports 13,033 affected and 912,171.227 person-hours, and Hedel/Alem/Heerewaarden ranks follow a hash rather than selected hydraulics.
findings.action: V3 release gate: require an expert-selected scenario contract with source river, gauge/datum/hydrograph, defence trajectory/state, breach/overtopping, LIWO scenario/edition, connected footprint, probability class, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, uncertainty, NoData and water-manager approval. Suppress local metre, affected, route and service claims until selected.

findings.summary: Generic water/drainage scores collapse rain-sewer overload, polder control, wastewater and drinking-water quantity/quality.
findings.evidence: E02 says intense rain overloads still-combined pipes; E03 assigns 244 partial objects with both supply and discharge functions, null/zero capacities and no topology; E04 prioritises drinking-water contamination. Pluvial T+24 nevertheless gives exact drainage 0.523542 and water 0.672123, while river T+72 gives 0.295371/0.387439 without catchment, pump, sewer, quality or operator state.
findings.action: Split surface-water supply/drainage, sewer conveyance/overflow, wastewater treatment and potable pressure/quantity/quality/advisory. Retain HWH objects as typed context until units, direction, duplication, connectivity, power, telemetry and valid state are governed. Missing or sensitive topology/state remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Four road identities cannot establish cross-river evacuation, village isolation, through-rail operation or external acute-care access.
findings.evidence: Six NWB records collapse to A2/N322/N831/N832; A2 and N322 are series dependencies. E04's evacuation routes and E06's official A2 closure example show that bridges, ramps, dike roads, load and valid time matter. There is no local station or emergency department; Jeroen Bosch and Rivierenland are external, and questionnaire/distance cannot establish reachability or acceptance.
findings.action: Build an internal multimodal reachability graph from NWB/BGT, authoritative bridges/sluices/ferries, ProRail and GTFS; bind NDW/operator state only by issue/valid/expiry time. Model self/assisted evacuation, responders, care, supply and repair separately, with route/destination capacity Unknown until confirmed.

findings.summary: Exact power, gas, telecom, facility and supply trajectories lack complete physical topology, live state, backup and restoration evidence.
findings.evidence: One Liander planning sample, 47 RDI installations, thirteen DUO locations, static transport and external hospitals are context only. They do not expose feeder/gas/pipe/backhaul topology, priority, load, switching, traffic, occupancy, stock, staff, generator endurance or restoration. Compound T+72 exposes exact availability from telecom 0.259597 to mobility 0.901733 without a named event or operator trajectory.
findings.action: Keep non-road services visibly synthetic with uncertainty. Ingest only operator-authorized service zones, dependencies and restoration ranges with publisher/version/time/coverage/licence and affectsSimulation. Planning territories and public points never imply physical flow or operational state.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour view lacks an accountable action/resource ledger and misuses an unconfirmed support network.
findings.evidence: E07 explicitly states no Maasdriel emergency support point exists; the Kerkdriel town hall is only the current contact fallback and support points are not shelters. E04 identifies unresolved care staffing, buffers, reachability and agreements. The model still outputs exact affected/service/recovery trajectories without confirmed warnings, evacuation, shelter/contact, water, care, stock, crew or restoration actions.
findings.action: At every checkpoint expose proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions with owner, authority, trigger, source, issue/valid/expiry time, geography, dependency, capacity/resource, confidence, verification and rollback. Label town hall fallback separately and never promote it or a school into shelter/support capacity without incident confirmation.

findings.summary: Resident vulnerability and external care capacity are reduced to false availability precision.
findings.evidence: CBS supports 21.1% age65-plus and 3,630 one-person households only as aggregates. E04 says flood-care staff reachability, buffers, cross-institution agreements and citizen access are insufficiently known; E06 has no local emergency department. Exact facilities availability and affected people-equivalent do not incorporate home care, medicine/device dependence, staff origin, transport or receiving capacity.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe aggregate care dependency, outreach, assisted-evacuation and destination-capacity states sourced from authorized GHOR/municipality/care partners. Keep staff, patient, home-care, pharmacy, ambulance, acceptance and generator state Unknown unless incident-confirmed; never target individuals from CBS aggregates.

findings.summary: Storm, coastal/wind, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake, wildfire/smoke and compound remain uncalibrated planning screens.
findings.evidence: E02/E04/E08 support severe weather, heat/drought, electricity/telecom/cyber and some nature-fire/smoke planning, while direct North Sea inundation and Groningen-style shaking are not local mechanisms. Coastal T+24 has zero water but 16.941 m/s wind; earthquake has zero T+24 motion but 3,915.070 person-hours; wildfire has zero local flame but smoke 0.351567. No named current event, forecast, plume, target or fragility is selected.
findings.action: Retain these as visibly synthetic exercises and separate direct local impact from remote/upstream effects. Require valid-time KNMI input/replay, named cyber target, selected earthquake/ground-motion surface and local ignition/perimeter/fuel/plume evidence before operational claims; zero, Unknown and not-applicable remain distinct.

findings.summary: Agriculture, greenhouse water quality and hazardous shipping pathways are absent from the canonical hazard/service vocabulary.
findings.evidence: E03/E08 identify intensive agriculture, greenhouse cultivation, bidirectional managed-water demand and 2025 pesticide exceedances; E04 prioritises a toxic shipping incident. Resident population and generic water/supply availability cannot represent livestock/crop/greenhouse demand, contaminated surface water, seasonal workers or river-shipping plume/exclusion effects.
findings.action: For later scope, add separately typed agriculture/greenhouse demand, water-quality advisories and hazardous-material plume/exclusion scenarios using authorized source, cargo/incident, wind, water and response evidence. Until then show Not modeled/Unknown, not normal water or safe transport.

findings.summary: Missing local sensors, forecast horizons, publication fields and operational registers need explicit multi-state semantics.
findings.evidence: GM0263 has 0/24 district-heating and charging values, four missing cars-per-household values, no local KNMI/RIVM PM2.5/seismic/Waterinfo point, no local emergency department and no national T+72 Waterinfo level forecast. HWH is partial; RDI/DUO/NBNL do not prove operation. These are Unknown/NoData, unlike the narrow model zeros for coastal water or T+24 ground motion.
findings.action: Use one map/API/export state contract: observed/modeled value including zero, Unknown/not covered, stale/expired and not applicable. Always show publisher, edition, issue/valid/retrieval time, units, coverage, completeness, licence, confidence and affectsSimulation; test that empty intersections, missing horizons, null CBS fields and masks never render safe/normal/zero.

findings.summary: The deterministic numerical and semantic contract passes for GM0263 on the audited build.
findings.evidence: The focused harness passes all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/bounded, zero-event behavior exact, all 24 neighbourhoods and 26,289 residents reconcile, demand/delivery and causal ledgers close, service selection leaves hazard unchanged, route flows stay within logical capacity and cumulative event-attributable burden is monotone.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, Waterschap Rivierenland, VRGZ, municipality or operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.

No expert-selected Waal, Maas or Afgedamde Maas gauge/hydrograph, trajectory, defence state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability class or NoData mask is ingested for GM0263.
The floodDepthM property and normalized inundation stress are derived screening values, not observed or officially modeled local metres and must not drive evacuation or route thresholds.
LIWO layers require native scenario edition, resolution, scope, mask/NoData, licence and water-manager interpretation; maximum or composite layers must not become automatic current scenarios.
The 107-position generalized boundary and common seed do not resolve river channels, defences, compartments, terrain, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, facilities, roads, households or individuals.
CBS neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; the -14 population difference and null district-heat, charging and car fields are publication semantics, not zero people/assets.

HWH is partial and its 244 points do not establish complete topology, compatible capacity units, control, live operation, power dependency, backup or restoration; registered zero and null remain source values.

Nearby Waterinfo values are point observations/forecasts tied to station/datum/time, not a municipal hydraulic surface, defence state or sewer condition; absent T+72 national level coverage is NoData.
No complete public causal Liander feeder/switching, Vitens/Dunea pipe/pressure/quality, gas district, municipal sewer, telecom backhaul or operator restoration topology is authorized in the model.
One NBNL postcode sample is large-user planning/queue context rather than municipality coverage, current load, customer outage, emergency reserve or restoration state.
RDI installations do not establish operator coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage, congestion, availability or restoration; fixed cadence and standard reuse licence are unstated.
NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static context and do not establish incident-time bridges, roads, trains, buses, throughput, evacuation, responder access or logistics continuity.
RIVM hospital questionnaire data and straight-line distances do not establish ambulance time, route access, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator fuel or backup endurance.
DUO locations do not establish command, reception, shelter, care or distribution roles; the municipality confirms no emergency support point and town hall is only a contact fallback.
The linked local heat plan's stated 2022–2025 validity has ended; current activation, partner capacity and a successor remain Unknown unless confirmed by Maasdriel/GGD.
Canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter, authoritative fuel/moisture, wind/plume, visitors, access and suppression-water evidence; remote smoke is not a local flame scenario.
Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path and detection/containment state; earthquake lacks a selected event, local ground-motion/site-response surface and fragility.
No local KNMI weather, RIVM PM2.5 or recent seismic point is available; nearest observations are not continuous local fields or forecasts through T+72.
Agriculture, greenhouse production, water-quality contamination, hazardous shipping and seasonal worker/visitor exposure are not represented by current resident/service aggregates.
Household 72-hour guidance is a preparedness horizon, not measured stock, guaranteed aid arrival, equality of access or a recovery deadline.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured customer outage-hours, people simultaneously without every service, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid change and 72 hours excludes prolonged flood, contamination, drought and reconstruction.

Gelderland/RWS/municipality/ProRail/OV/VRGZ/care partners: validate A2 Waal/Maas bridges, N322 and dike-road/sluice/ferry alternatives, through-rail/bus continuity, evacuation pickup/destination capacity and time-dependent access to Jeroen Bosch/Rivierenland; static geometry and questionnaires do not prove continuity.
